chunks: And it is narrated from 'A'idh al-Ahmasi that he said:

I entered upon Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام while I intended to ask him about salat (prayer), but he began with me and said: "If you meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with the five prayers, He will not ask you about anything besides them."

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu 'Abdillah, Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being asked about
key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the One before Whom the servant is ultimately brought
key_terms.بِالصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسِ: with the five daily prayers, meaning fulfillment of the obligatory daily salat
key_terms.سِوَاهُنَّ: other than them, meaning anything besides the five prayers
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: the Mighty and Majestic, an honorific description of Allah
key_terms.لَمْ يَسْأَلْكَ: He will not ask you, indicating freedom from further questioning in this context

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about meeting Allah with the five daily prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the immense importance of faithfully performing the five daily salat (prayers). It presents these obligatory prayers as a central act of worship through which a servant meets Allah عزّ وجلّ, highlighting their decisive significance in one's reckoning.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.615 - It is narrated from 'Aidh al-Amasi that He said:

"I entered upon Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) with the intention of asking him about prayer.
Imam (as) began speaking before I could ask and said: 'If you meet Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, with the five daily prayers, He will not ask you about anything else.'".
